correctness.rationale: The exact sentence theta_j has occurrence probability 1-(1-p_nj)^c_n, and the uniformly valid exponential approximation makes convergence of this probability equivalent to convergence of c_np_nj in the extended interval. For any quantifier rank q, the EF game on equal truncated per-class color populations and per-profile class counts preserves all q-rank sentences. For large s_n profiles reduce to 2q rare colors and one typical color; multinomial joint rare-category Poisson limits and concentration of diverging categories give a limiting truncated profile vector. Every FO sentence has finite rank. The zero-one criterion is necessary by theta_j and sufficient by deterministic profile limits. This is deductive; finite code verifies exact identities only.

value.rationale: The problem is prompted by a concrete foundational gap in random expansions of deterministic finite bases: it identifies, for unrestricted growth schedules, an exact iff condition for the entire FO limit law, a sharp zero-one boundary and critical independent Poisson behavior. Explicit oscillating expansions show that even bases with the same eventual complete FO reduct theory may lose convergence. This structural phase classification is natural and reusable, not an arbitrary tiny finite slice.
